current_object.statement:
Let the laboratory region, its inertial chart and the fields and sources be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-sources]], with the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; fix the ordered basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of the chart and the oriented volume form $\varepsilon$ of [[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]], with $\varepsilon_{0123}=+1$ and $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. current_object.title: The static and pure electrostatic regimes and their fixed-time reading
current_object.statement:
Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the units, constants and symbols of [[def-em-si-conventions]], let $E:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ and $B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be fields of [[def-em-fields]] and let $(\rho,J)$ be source fields of [[def-em-sources]] on $\Omega\times I$, all of class $C^1$ (with every additional derivative appearing below existing and continuous); $\partial_t$ is the partial time derivative at fixed position of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]].
(a) [Static regime] The **static (time-independent) electromagnetic regime** on $\Omega\times I$ is the requirement
$$\partial_tE=0,\qquad\partial_tB=0,\qquad\partial_t\rho=0,\qquad\partial_tJ=0\qquad\text{on }\Omega\times I.$$
(b) [Pure electrostatics] The **pure electrostatic regime** is the static regime together with $J=0$ and $B=0$ on $\Omega\times I$.
(c) [Reduced equations] If the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] holds in the static regime, then the four Maxwell equations reduce to
$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad\operatorname{curl}E=0,\qquad\operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J$$
pointwise on $\Omega\times I$, with $\operatorname{div}$ and $\operatorname{curl}$ of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] applied at each fixed time; in the pure electrostatic regime the reduction is exactly the pair $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=0$.
(d) [Fixed-time reading] In the static regime $E,B,\rho,J$ do not depend on $t$, so each is the pullback along $(y,t)\mapsto y$ of a single map on $\Omega$; this fixed-time reading (the spatial field or source) is the object analysed by the electrostatic statements of this page, and no other time dependence is introduced. The equations of (c) are equations between those spatial maps.
(e) [Static-to-distributional reading] Let fields $E,B$ and volume densities $\rho,J$ be locally integrable and time independent on $\Omega\times I$, and let $\Omega$ be open. Then, under the $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention of the cited measure and distribution interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]), the weak equations of the solution predicate of [[def-em-weak-sources]](e) for these time-independent objects hold if and only if the four spatial equations $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=0$, $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J$ hold in $\mathcal D'(\Omega)$; the passage between them is the integration in $t$ of the pairings against $C_c^\infty(I\times\Omega)$ tests, justified by [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] after identifying fields and densities with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]). In particular a **stationary point charge** at $x_0\in\Omega$ with charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$ is the point source of [[def-em-weak-sources]](b) with constant trajectory $z(t)\equiv x_0$, whose pairing is $\psi\mapsto q\int_I\psi(x_0,t)\,dt$ and whose fixed-time reading is the spatial point source $\eta\mapsto q\eta(x_0)$ ([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]).
(f) [Conventions and scope] The regime is imposed in the one inertial frame of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]; no claim is made that time independence survives a change of inertial description, and where a frame change is used the transformed fields must be rechecked. The static regime is an adopted idealization, not a dynamical stability theorem: static charged matter requires external support or an adopted equilibrium model. No equation is asserted here for singular sources beyond the dictionary of (e), and no empirical claim is made.
current_object.strategy: For the locally integrable branch use Borel representatives of each spatial component, obtained under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ from [[cor-lebesgue-sigma-algebra-is-the-completion-of-borel-lebesgue-measure]] and [[thm-completion-measurable-functions-have-base-measurable-representatives]] after zero extension outside $\Omega$. These changes are on spatial null sets and their products with compact time intervals are null, so they do not change spatial or spacetime regular distributions. With [[thm-borel-products-of-euclidean-spaces-are-euclidean-borel]] and [[thm-lebesgue-product-measure-agrees-with-euclidean-lebesgue-on-borel-sets]], the pairings may therefore be evaluated using the product measure and Fubini below. A convention definition with the two elementary verifications (c) and (e). For (c): substituting $\partial_tE=\partial_tB=0$ into $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$ of the smooth branch ([[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]) gives $\operatorname{curl}E=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J$ at each fixed time, while $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and $\operatorname{div}B=0$ are the unchanged divergence equations; the identification of the operators at fixed time is that of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], applied to the fixed-time fields of [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-sources]]. In the pure case $B=0$, $J=0$ this pair reads $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=0$, which are identities. For (d): time independence makes $(y,t)\mapsto F(y,t)$ the composition of $(y,t)\mapsto y$ with $y\mapsto F(y,t_0)$ for any fixed $t_0$; that the fixed-time value is independent of $t_0$ uses only the vanishing of all the $\partial_t$'s and the differentiability convention of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]] (a $C^1$ function on the interval $I$ with zero derivative is constant, cf. the mean-value theorem for the single variable $t$). For (e): write the four pairings of [[def-em-weak-sources]](e) with $\psi\in C_c^\infty(I\times\Omega)$; for each fixed $t$ the map $\psi(\cdot,t)$ has compact support in a fixed compact subset of $\Omega$ and lies in $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$, so the spatial distributional equation evaluated at $\psi(\cdot,t)$ gives the identity for the inner integral; integrating over $t$ with [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] (for a compact test supported in $K\times T\Subset\Omega\times I$, each absolute field/density pairing is bounded by $C_\psi\mathbf1_T(t)|F(y)|\mathbf1_K(y)$, whose integral is at most $C_\psi|T|\int_K|F|<\infty$ since $F\in L^1_{\rm loc}$; continuity of $F$ is not required) produces the four-dimensional pairing. For each time-independent component $F$, the time derivative pairing is zero: $\langle\partial_tT_F,\psi\rangle=-\int_K F(y)(\int_I\partial_t\psi(y,t)dt)dy=0$, using the same absolute majorant, Fubini and the fundamental theorem with compact time support. Thus the Faraday and Ampere time terms vanish distributionally. Conversely, testing with $\psi(y,t)=\eta(y)\chi(t)$ for $\eta\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$, $\chi\in C_c^\infty(I)$ with $\int\chi=1$ recovers the spatial equations, using that all objects are time independent. The point-charge dictionary is the specialisation of [[def-em-weak-sources]](b) to the constant trajectory $z\equiv x_0$, which is $C^1$, proper into $U$ (its graph is $\{x_0\}\times I$, whose preimages of compact sets are compact), and whose pairings reduce to $q\int_I\psi(x_0,t)\,dt=\langle q\delta_{x_0},\int_I\psi(\cdot,t)\,dt\rangle$; the spatial point source $q\delta_{x_0}$ is that of [[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]. Clause (f) records the frame dependence and the idealization; no boost statement and no dynamics are asserted, so nothing beyond the cited definitions and the two integrations is used. Finite-interval integrations of the continuous one-variable test/radial integrands above use [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]] to identify their Riemann/FTC values with their Lebesgue values before Fubini, polar integration or passage to improper limits; real and imaginary test components are treated separately.

current_object.title: The electric and magnetic fields as fixed-time spatial vector fields
current_object.statement: Let the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$, its spatial Euclidean structure and its units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $k\ge1$. An electric field of class $C^k$ on the region is a map $E:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ that is of class $C^k$ in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]; a magnetic field of class $C^k$ is a map $B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ of the same class. At fixed $t\in I$ the maps $E(\cdot,t),B(\cdot,t):\Omega\to\mathbb R^3$ are real spatial vector fields on the region $\Omega$, read in the $\delta$-orthonormal basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of the frame. The framework uses: $C^1$ fields in the classical Maxwell branch, $C^2$ fields where second or mixed time-space derivatives of the fields appear, and $C^\infty$ fields in the smooth existence branches; every statement carries its own regularity and no regularity beyond it is asserted. Conventions: (a) $E$ is a polar vector and $B$ an axial vector relative to the orientation of the spatial basis; the changes of inertial description adopted in [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] are proper and orientation preserving, so orientation-reversing descriptions are not among them; (b) the fields are defined by their values on $\Omega\times I$, and no value at a point of singular source support is asserted; (c) $E$ carries V m$^{-1}$ and $B$ carries T; (d) the identification of the pair $(E,B)$ with the components of an alternating two-form, including its transformation behaviour, is made in [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] and is not presupposed here.
current_object.strategy: An explicit type/domain/convention definition: the fields are maps on the product $\Omega\times I$ of the laboratory region with a stated class of regularity, and their fixed-time readings are spatial vector fields in the frame basis. The regularity notion is that of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]; the polar/axial convention and the exclusion of pointwise values at singular source support are conventions recorded explicitly rather than used implicitly. No differential equation and no derived quantity is introduced by this definition.

current_object.title: Laboratory geometry: a restricted inertial chart, its spatial slices and fixed-time fields
current_object.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be an oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), let $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame with inertial chart $x:A\to\mathbb R^4$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]), let $c>0$ be the framework's conversion constant, and let $\delta$ be the Euclidean spatial form of that frame on $n^\perp$, $n:=e_0$, with norm $|\cdot|$ and positive spatial orientation ([[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]). Fix a nonempty open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ ([[def-interval]]) and a nonempty open set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, and put

$$U:=\{p\in A:\ \text{there are }t\in I,\ y\in\Omega\text{ with }x^0(p)=ct,\ (x^1,x^2,x^3)(p)=y\}.$$

Then: (a) [Chart restriction] $x(U)=\{(ct,y):t\in I,\ y\in\Omega\}$ and $\Phi:U\to I\times\Omega$, $\Phi(p):=(x^0(p)/c,(x^1,x^2,x^3)(p))$, is a bijection, because the inertial chart $x:A\to\mathbb R^4$ is a bijection and $c>0$; its components are the laboratory time coordinate $t(p):=x^0(p)/c$ and the laboratory position $r(p):=(x^1(p),x^2(p),x^3(p))$. (b) [Slices and spatial structure] For each $t\in I$ the slice $U_t:=\{p\in U:t(p)=t\}$ is carried bijectively onto $\Omega$ by $r$; the constant vector $n=e_0$ is future unit timelike, and $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is the $\delta$-orthonormal positively oriented basis of $n^\perp$ in which the coordinates of $r$ are expressed. (c) [Laboratory fields] A laboratory field of rank $m$ is a map $F:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^m$; it is identified with the map $U\to\mathbb R^m$, $p\mapsto F(r(p),t(p))$, and with the family $(F(\cdot,t))_{t\in I}$ of maps $\Omega\to\mathbb R^m$, its values at fixed time. Such a field is of class $C^k$ when the map $(y,t)\mapsto F(y,t)$ is $C^k$ in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]; then $\partial_{y_i}F$ (at fixed $t$) and $\partial_tF$ (at fixed $y$) are the partial derivatives of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. No regularity of a field is asserted beyond the class stated for it. (d) [Conventions] The product decomposition is a coordinate identification inside the single inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$; it is not a Galilean transformation, it does not compare two inertial frames, and it does not assert absolute simultaneity. The objects $I,\Omega,t,r,\delta$ and the identification $\mathbb R^3\cong n^\perp$ belong to the named frame; changes of inertial description are the proper orthochronous maps adopted in [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]]. The frame is an origin together with an ordered basis; it is not a congruence of observers, and no moving observer field is defined here.
current_object.strategy: A construction definition with elementary verifications. The inertial chart $x$ of [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]] is a bijection, so its restriction to the set of events whose chart coordinates lie in $cI\times\Omega$ has image $cI\times\Omega$; composing with the bijection $cI\times\Omega\to I\times\Omega$, $(ct,y)\mapsto(t,y)$ (bijective because $c>0$) gives the bijection $\Phi$. Each slice $U_t$ is $\Phi^{-1}(\{t\}\times\Omega)$, on which $r$ restricts to a bijection onto $\Omega$. The claims about $n$, $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$, $\delta$ and the orientation are exactly the content of [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]; the $C^k$ notion is that of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]] and the two kinds of partial derivative are those of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]] applied to the product coordinates. Clause (d) records conventions only: the frame dependence of $r,\delta$ and slices is stated rather than hidden, and no Galilean or observer-congruence claim is made. Nothing here uses a theorem of the framework, and the laboratory region may be a proper subset of $A$; no global chart of $A$ other than the given inertial chart is asserted.

current_object.title: Worldlines, four-velocity, chart readings and the frame/observer distinction
current_object.statement: The particle and light objects of the framework are the following curves and vector fields of the affine Minkowski model ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]), with the physical interpretation of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]] and the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. (a) [Worldlines] A worldline is a regular causal curve $x:J\to A$ in one of the regularity classes of [[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]] ($J$ an order-convex subset of $\mathbb R$ with at least two elements). A massive worldline is a $C^k$ future timelike worldline, $k\ge1$, with everywhere nonzero future timelike tangent; a light ray is a $C^1$ future null curve with everywhere nonzero future null tangent. A null curve has zero proper-time increment along every subinterval and no proper-time parametrization ([[def-sr-proper-time]]), and it is never treated as a massive worldline. A worldline is a curve in spacetime; its reading $r\circ x$ in a named laboratory chart is a coordinate description of it, not an object of another observer. (b) [Four-velocity and four-acceleration] For a massive worldline the four-velocity $U$ and, when it is $C^2$, the four-acceleration $A$ are those of [[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]; wherever defined they satisfy $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ and $\eta(U,A)=0$, by [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]. (c) [Chart reading] If a massive $C^2$ worldline has laboratory reading $t\mapsto r(t)$ in a chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], then $|r'(t)|<c$ for every $t$, with four-velocity $U=\gamma(c,r')$ and Lorentz factor $\gamma=(1-|r'|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, by clause (e) of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]. (d) [Frames and observers] An inertial frame in this framework is the origin-with-basis object of [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]; a point observer is a future unit timelike vector $n\in V$ with rest space $n^\perp$ and rest projection $h$, as in clauses (c)-(d) of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]. An observer congruence and a noninertial tetrad field are further objects, not defined by this item; the words 'frame', 'chart', 'observer' and 'tetrad' denote distinct notions and are not interchangeable. (e) [Scope] No force law, no self-field and no extended-body structure is supplied here; an accelerating massive worldline requires a force model stated separately, and an ideal light ray carries no dispersive, quantum or polarisation structure in this definition.
current_object.strategy: A definition reusing the special-relativity curve notions with their exact statements rather than restating them: regularity and causal character of curves are those of [[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]; proper time and its non-applicability to null curves are those of [[def-sr-proper-time]]; $U$ and $A$ are those of [[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]; the identities $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$, $\eta(U,A)=0$, the chart bound $|r'|<c$ and the velocity reading $U=\gamma(c,r')$ are the exact clauses of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]. The frame/observer distinction is the one of [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]] together with the rest-space and projection clauses of the same theorem. The item adds the physical interpretation adopted in [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]] and records the scope exclusions; it proves no dynamical statement.

current_object.title: Framework-local SI units, the vacuum constants and the exact/measured status of their values
current_object.statement: Adopt the SI system of units for this framework, with the following quantity table and conventions; every symbol is a quantity of this framework and the laboratory structure is that of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]. (a) [Coordinates and constants] $x^0=ct$ and each spatial coordinate $x^i$ carries the metre (m); the time coordinate $t$ carries the second (s); the conversion constant $c>0$ carries m s$^{-1}$ and has the exact SI defining value $c=299\,792\,458\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the elementary charge $e$ has the exact SI defining value $e=1.602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm{C}$, and this item does not assert that physical charge is quantised; the magnetic constant $\mu_0>0$ carries N A$^{-2}$ and is measured, so no exact numerical value of $\mu_0$ is asserted (the pre-2019 SI fixed the historical nominal $\mu_{0,\mathrm{nom}}:=4\pi\times10^{-7}\ \mathrm{H\,m^{-1}}=4\pi\times10^{-7}\ \mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$ exactly; since the revised SI took effect on 20 May 2019, $\mu_0$ is experimentally determined. The SI brochure quotes the nominal $\mu_{0,\mathrm{nom}}$ as the estimate at the 2019 adoption with relative standard uncertainty $2.3\times10^{-10}$; this is historical estimate/uncertainty context, not an exact equality for the actual $\mu_0$ or a current measured value); the electric constant is defined within the framework by $\varepsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ in F m$^{-1}$, consistent with the exact SI relation $\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1/c^2$, so that $c^2\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1$ and $\varepsilon_0$ inherits the relative standard uncertainty of $\mu_0$. (b) [Electromagnetic quantities] Charge $q$ carries the coulomb (C); the charge density $\rho$ of [[def-em-sources]] carries C m$^{-3}$ and the current density $J$ carries A m$^{-2}$, so that the four-current components $(c\rho,J)$ carry A m$^{-2}$; the electric field $E$ carries V m$^{-1}$; the magnetic field $B$ carries the tesla (T), where $1\ \mathrm{T}=1\ \mathrm{N\,A^{-1}\,m^{-1}}$; the scalar potential $\varphi$ carries V and the vector potential $A$ carries T m, so that the four-potential components $(\varphi/c,A)$ carry T m; the components of the electromagnetic two-form of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] carry T; a force carries the newton (N), $1\ \mathrm{N}=1\ \mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}}$. (c) [Mechanical quantities] A rest mass parameter $m$ carries the kilogram (kg) and a four-momentum $P=mU$ carries kg m s$^{-1}$ ([[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]]); field energy density carries J m$^{-3}$, energy flux W m$^{-2}$, so that $1\ \mathrm{W}=1\ \mathrm{J\,s^{-1}}=1\ \mathrm{V\,A}$. (d) [Bookkeeping only] The unit of a quantity records the adopted system of units; it does not show that a quantity is primitive in this or any other framework, it contains no measurement, and it does not identify a quantity with a similarly named quantity of another framework. The exact defining values of $c$ and $e$ fix numerical conventions of the SI, they do not by themselves identify $c$ with the vacuum propagation constant of ideal light, which is the physical adoption of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]].
current_object.strategy: A convention definition: it fixes the coordinate normalisation $x^0=ct$, the unit of each quantity used in this framework, the exact SI defining values of $c$ and $e$ and the measured status of $\mu_0$. The exact values $c=299\,792\,458$ m/s and $e=1.602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}$ C, and the statements that the new definition of the ampere fixes $e$ rather than $\mu_0$, that $\mu_0$ must now be determined experimentally, and that $\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1/c^2$ remains exact, are taken from the SI brochure's defining-constants table and its ampere section. The framework's definition of $\varepsilon_0$ by $(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ is a definition consistent with that exact relation; the uncertainty carried by $\varepsilon_0$ is recorded rather than hidden. The dimensional checks of the framework's equations and couplings are developed on the companion examples page of this pair. No exact or current measured numerical value of $\mu_0$ is asserted and no experiment is claimed. The historical nominal and adoption uncertainty are explicitly source context, not a substitution for the current experimentally determined constant.

current_object.title: Charge parameter, frame charge and current densities, volume charge and flux, and the four-current
current_object.statement:
Let the laboratory region and its chart be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. (a) [Charge parameter] The framework takes a real charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$, measured in coulombs, attached to a source; its sign is the sign of the source and it is a parameter of the model. Charge quantisation is not asserted. (b) [Smooth source fields] A smooth (volume) source field on $\Omega\times I$ is a pair $(\rho,J)$ of maps $\rho:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$, $J:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ that is continuous on $\Omega\times I$ and of class $C^1$ wherever a displayed equation differentiates it; $\rho$ is the frame charge density (C m$^{-3}$) and $J$ the frame current density (A m$^{-2}$). For each fixed $t\in I$ retain the compact Jordan branch: if $V\subseteq\Omega$ is compact and Jordan measurable, define $Q_R(V,t):=\int_V\rho(y,t)dy$ by [[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]], with integrability supplied by [[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]]. For the full measurable-volume branch assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), as required by the published Lebesgue-measure interface. If $V$ is any bounded Lebesgue-measurable subset with compact closure $\overline V\subseteq\Omega$, define
$$Q(V,t):=\int_V\rho(y,t)d\lambda_3(y)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}F_t(y)\mathbf1_V(y)d\lambda_3(y),$$
where $F_t=\rho(\cdot,t)$ on $\Omega$ and $0$ elsewhere; the signed integral is defined through its positive and negative parts ([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]). This integral is absolutely finite, since $\rho(\cdot,t)$ is bounded on $\overline V$ and $V$ has finite Lebesgue measure. On the compact Jordan branch, under the same Countable Choice assumption, $Q=Q_R$ by [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]]. The empty region has charge zero in both branches. The current flux remains defined independently: for each oriented surface patch in $\Omega$ with unit normal field $n_S$ the current flux at time $t$ is $\int_S J(y,t)\cdot n_S(y)\,dS$ ([[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]]). Point sources and sheet sources are not source fields in this sense; they are different objects, defined by their own pairings when the framework uses them. (c) [Covariant identification] Write $j:=(c\rho,J)$, so $j^0=c\rho$ and $j^i=J^i$. The framework adopts as a model premise the identification of the charge-current of a source with a vector field of the affine Minkowski model, and hence the component transformation law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] for $j$ between inertial charts. This is a model premise, not a theorem about physical currents. (d) [Frame density, scalar multiplier and the normalized material branch] Suppose additionally that the identified $j$ is $C^1$ and $j=\rho_0U$, with a $C^1$ future timelike vector field $U$ and a $C^1$ real scalar multiplier $\rho_0$. Since $U^0>0$, define the normalized chart direction $u:=U/U^0$, so $u^0=1$, $u^i=U^i/U^0$. Then $j=(\rho_0U^0)u$ and, because the electromagnetic convention is $j^0=c\rho$,
$$\rho=\rho_0U^0/c,\qquad J^i=\rho_0U^i=c\rho\,u^i.$$
Pointwise equality $\rho=\rho_0$ holds if and only if $\rho_0(U^0-c)=0$, including the zero-multiplier case. Where $\rho_0\ne0$, equality is equivalent to $U^0=c$, which does not alone imply $U^i=0$ for an arbitrary future timelike $U$. Thus a scalar multiplier is not automatically a Lorentz rest charge density. The direction $u$ is chart normalized, with no unit or proper-four-velocity normalization imposed in this general branch; if its coordinate velocity interpretation is adopted, the spatial velocity is $v^i:=cu^i$.
For the separate convective source model, explicitly assume that $U$ is the material proper-time four-velocity, normalized by $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ as in [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]. This is an additional model condition, not a consequence of the factorization $j=\rho_0U$. In that branch, $U=\gamma(c,v)$, $|v|<c$, $\gamma=(1-|v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, and
$$\rho=\gamma\rho_0,\qquad J=\rho v.$$
Here $\rho_0$ is the rest charge density of this stipulated convective model: in a comoving inertial frame $U=(c,0,0,0)$ and $j=(c\rho_0,0,0,0)$. The equality $\rho=\rho_0$ then holds exactly where $\rho_0=0$ or $v=0$ (equivalently $\gamma=1$). Both signs of charge and the zero-density case are retained. (e) [Scope] This definition fixes the source objects of the smooth branch and their transformation interface. It asserts no conservation law (that is proved for stated source classes) and no regularity of singular sources.
current_object.strategy:
Keep clauses (a)-(c) as explicit source types and the adopted physical identification. The compact Jordan branch uses [[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]] and [[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]]; flux uses [[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]]. For the broader Lebesgue branch assume the explicitly stated Countable Choice, without Dependent Choice or a convergence/FTC assumption. Fix $t$ and an admitted nonempty $V$. The continuous function $\rho(\cdot,t)$ is bounded by $M_t<\infty$ in absolute value on compact $\overline V$ by [[thm-extreme-value-metric]]. Its zero extension $F_t$ is Borel: for every open $O\subseteq\mathbb R$, the inverse image inside the open set $\Omega$ is relatively open and hence open in $\mathbb R^3$; add the closed complement of $\Omega$ precisely when $0\in O$. This is also the open-set form of [[thm-continuous-preimages-of-borel-sets-are-borel]]. Under Countable Choice, Borel sets are Lebesgue measurable ([[thm-borel-sets-are-lebesgue-measurable]]) and bounded measurable $V$ has finite measure ([[prop-lebesgue-measure-is-sigma-finite-and-finite-on-bounded-sets]]). Positive/negative parts and their restrictions by $\mathbf1_V$ are measurable by [[prop-closure-properties-of-measurable-functions-used-by-the-integral]]. The bound $|F_t|\mathbf1_V\le M_t\mathbf1_V$ and [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]] give
$$\int|F_t|\mathbf1_Vd\lambda_3\le M_t\lambda_3(V)<\infty,$$
where the indicator integral is its simple-function value by [[prop-the-nonnegative-integral-agrees-with-the-simple-integral]]. This proves exactly the absolute signed integrability required by [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]] and defines $Q$ using the nonnegative restrictions of [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]. For empty $V$ the product is zero. On compact Jordan $V$, the continuous density restricted to V has a bounded Borel zero extension to a bounding rectangle, so the exact compact-Jordan clause of [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]], also under Countable Choice, identifies the two finite integral values. The algebraic supplier [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]](vii) gives $j=\rho_0U=\rho_0U^0u$; its coordinate density is $j^0$, whereas the present SI source convention defines $j^0=c\rho$. Division by $c>0$ gives $\rho=\rho_0U^0/c$ and $\rho-\rho_0=\rho_0(U^0-c)/c$, proving exactly the stated equality cases. The spatial components give $J^i=c\rho u^i$. Neither $U^0=c$ nor chart normalization $u^0=1$ is a proper-four-velocity condition.
In the additional normalized material model, write $v=c(U^1,U^2,U^3)/U^0$. The norm equation $-(U^0)^2+|U_{\mathrm{sp}}|^2=-c^2$ gives $(U^0)^2(1-|v|^2/c^2)=c^2$, and future timelikeness gives $U^0>0$ and $|v|<c$, so $U^0=c\gamma$. This is the exact four-velocity/relative-velocity content of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]; substitution gives $\rho=\gamma\rho_0$ and $J=\rho v$. In its comoving frame $U^0=c$, hence the source convention identifies the scalar multiplier with the stipulated rest-frame density. Since $\gamma=1$ if and only if $v=0$, the normalized equality cases follow, including $\rho_0=0$. All density readings remain within the adopted current model; no conservation, measurement, general current factorization, force law or singular-source regularity is deduced.

current_object.title: Outgoing spherical radial functions: exact bounds on the spherical Dirichlet-to-Neumann coefficient
current_object.statement: For $l\in\mathbb N_0$ and $z>0$ set $$h_l(z)=(-i)^{l+1}\frac{e^{iz}}{z}\sum_{j=0}^{l}\frac{i^j\,(l+j)!}{j!\,(l-j)!\,(2z)^j}.$$ Then $h_l$ is a complex-valued $C^2$ function of $z>0$ solving $$h_l''(z)+\frac2z h_l'(z)+\Bigl[1-\frac{l(l+1)}{z^2}\Bigr]h_l(z)=0,$$ it never vanishes on $(0,\infty)$, and its Wronskian-type identity $\operatorname{Im}\bigl(\overline{h_l(z)}\,h_l'(z)\bigr)=z^{-2}$ holds. For $k>0$ and $R>0$ the spherical Dirichlet-to-Neumann coefficient $$t_l=\frac{k\,h_l'(kR)}{h_l(kR)}$$ satisfies the exact bounds $$\operatorname{Re}t_l\le-\frac1R,\qquad |\operatorname{Re}t_l|\le\frac{l+1}{R},\qquad 0<\operatorname{Im}t_l\le k .$$ These are exact identities and inequalities for the displayed explicit functions, not asymptotic formulas; the argument uses only elementary differentiation and a constant Wronskian, so no large-$l$ asymptotic input is required.
current_object.strategy: Substituting $h=e^{iz}P(z)/z$ with $P(z)=\sum_{j=0}^l b_jz^{-j}$ into the radial equation gives the coefficient recursion $b_{j+1}=i(l+j+1)(l-j)b_j/[2(j+1)]$ with $b_0=1$, terminating at $j=l$ because $l-j=0$; its solution is the displayed factorial formula, which proves the equation and shows the leading outgoing term $(-i)^{l+1}e^{iz}/z$ with a finite remainder. Writing $y=zh_l$ gives $y''+(1-l(l+1)z^{-2})y=0$ with real coefficient; differentiating $\operatorname{Im}(\overline y\,y')$ and using the equation shows its derivative is zero, so by the zero-derivative-implies-constant corollary on the interval $(0,\infty)$ ([[cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant]]) it is constant, and its large-$z$ leading exponential gives the constant $1$: hence $\operatorname{Im}(\overline{h_l}h_l')=z^{-2}\ne0$, so $h_l$ never vanishes. For the real bounds set $F=|y|^2=|P|^2$; since $b_j$ carries phase $i^j$ times a real number, odd cross terms cancel and $F$ is an even finite polynomial in $z^{-1}$, $F=\sum_{j\ge0}a_jz^{-2j}$ with $a_0=1$. Differentiating the real equation gives $F'''+4(1-l(l+1)z^{-2})F'+4l(l+1)Fz^{-3}=0$, whose coefficient matching yields $a_{j+1}=(2j+1)[l(l+1)-j(j+1)]a_j/[2(j+1)]$, all positive for $0\le j\le l$ and zero at $j=l+1$, with the closed form $a_j=(2j)!(l+j)!/[2^{2j}(j!)^2(l-j)!]$. Thus $|h_l|^2=z^{-2}\sum a_jz^{-2j}\ge z^{-2}$ and half the logarithmic derivative gives $\operatorname{Re}[kh_l'/h_l]=-R^{-1}\bigl[\sum_ja_j(kR)^{-2j}+\sum_j j a_j(kR)^{-2j}\bigr]/\sum_ja_j(kR)^{-2j}$, a weighted average of $j\in\{0,\dots,l\}$, so it lies in $[-\,(l+1)/R,\,-1/R]$. The Wronskian identity gives $\operatorname{Im}[kh_l'(kR)/h_l(kR)]=k/(k^2R^2\,|h_l(kR)|^2)=k/(k^2R^2|h_l|^2)\in(0,k]$ using $|h_l|^2\ge z^{-2}$. The derivative computations use the algebra of derivatives and the entireness of the complex exponential ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]]).

current_object.title: Outgoing spherical trace and Dirichlet-to-Neumann map
current_object.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the explicitly used trace and weak Dirichlet-solvability suppliers. Let $k>0$ and $R>0$. Use the sphere-normalised basis $Y^R_{lm}(Rn):=R^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$ on $S_R$, where $Y_{lm}$ is the complete normalised unit-sphere basis of the spherical-harmonic lemma ([[lem-em-spherical-harmonic-basis-and-addition]]) and the coefficients $t_l$ of the outgoing radial-function lemma ([[lem-em-outgoing-spherical-hankel-dtn-bounds]]). The map $$T_Rf=\sum_{l,m}t_l\,f_{lm}Y^R_{lm},\qquad f\in H^{1/2}(S_R),$$ is a bounded linear operator $H^{1/2}(S_R)\to H^{-1/2}(S_R)$ with $$\operatorname{Re}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle\le0,\qquad \operatorname{Im}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle=\sum_{l,m}(\operatorname{Im}t_l)|f_{lm}|^2>0\ \ (f\ne0).$$ It is precisely the outgoing scalar Helmholtz normal derivative at $r=R$: for every $f\in H^{1/2}(S_R)$ the function $u(rn)=\sum_{l,m}f_{lm}h_l(kr)/h_l(kR)\,R^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$ for $r\ge R$ is the unique outgoing finite-local-energy exterior solution with trace $f$ on $S_R$ and normal derivative $T_Rf$ in the weak trace sense; it is smooth away from the sphere, and for smooth $f$ it satisfies the ordinary Sommerfeld condition. No uniform pointwise outgoing condition is asserted for arbitrary rough traces; the outgoing condition there is its modal/weak version. Here finite-local-energy means membership in $H^1(\{R<|x|<R_1\})$ for every finite $R_1>R$, with the $H^{1/2}$ trace on $S_R$; no global $H^1$ or global $L^2$ condition at infinity is imposed. The outgoing modal class consists of the displayed outgoing $h_l$ radial factors with no incoming partners; for rough traces this modal class is the definition, rather than a pointwise Sommerfeld assertion. Here the boundary Sobolev spaces are their complex versions (or complexifications of the real trace spaces), $f_{lm}=\int_{S_R}f\overline{Y^R_{lm}}\,d\sigma_R$, and the DtN dual pairing is linear in its first argument and conjugate-linear in its second.
current_object.strategy: The boundary norm of the fractional Sobolev space is equivalent, for fixed $R$, to $\sum_{l,m}(l+1)|f_{lm}|^2$: for finite harmonic data the harmonic ball extension $\sum_{l,m}(r/R)^lf_{lm}R^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$ has Dirichlet energy $\sum(l/R)|f_{lm}|^2$ by the first Green identity ([[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]) and normal differentiation, and $L^2$ ball norm $\sum R/(2l+3)|f_{lm}|^2$ with the sphere-normalised basis, so its $H^1$ norm is equivalent to $\sum(l+1)|f_{lm}|^2$. For arbitrary $H^{1/2}$ data the bounded right inverse and the weak harmonic Dirichlet solver of the prescribed-data lemma ([[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]]) give a controlled harmonic $H^1$ extension; the harmonic coefficients and orthogonality of the ball Poisson series lemma ([[lem-em-ball-poisson-series-boundary-convergence]]) show the finite energy partial sums are bounded by its energy, giving both directions of the equivalence. The bounds $|t_l|\le(l+1)/R+k$ of the spherical Hankel lemma ([[lem-em-outgoing-spherical-hankel-dtn-bounds]]) make $T_R$ bounded into the dual weighted space, and the real and imaginary pairings converge with the stated signs, strict positivity following from $\operatorname{Im}t_l>0$ for every $l$. For the exterior realisation, define $u_{lm}(r)=f_{lm}h_l(kr)/h_l(kR)$, $r\ge R$; the finite polynomial positive formula gives $|h_l(kr)/h_l(kR)|\le R/r$ and, by the recurrence, geometric-in-$l$ radial ratios on every compact $r>R$ interval, so the series and all derivatives converge uniformly there, away from the sphere; the smoothness, the weak trace identification and the annular $H^1$ control follow from Green's identity for each mode on $[R,R+\delta]$ and the bounds above. Uniqueness: the general radial Helmholtz solutions are multiples of $h_l(kr)$ and its incoming partner, whose Wronskian is nonzero; Sommerfeld selects $h_l$, and harmonic completeness forces any smooth outgoing exterior solution to have exactly this map. The annular $H^1$ estimates are precisely the finite-local-energy condition; they do not assert global integrability at infinity. At $l=0$, a nonzero outgoing mode is proportional to $e^{ikr}/r$ and its global $L^2$ norm diverges, which confirms why no global energy condition is imposed. Both the ball and exterior radial extensions use $R^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$ explicitly; the sphere-normalisation is $Y^R_{lm}(Rn)=R^{-1}Y_{lm}(n)$, giving the stated radial ball-norm factor $R/(2l+3)$ for the sphere-normalised coefficients. For complex boundary data, apply the real prescribed-trace/harmonic solver to the real and imaginary parts and combine; the resulting squared norm is the sum of the two real energy norms, with the stated sesquilinear pairing.

current_object.title: The Lorentz coupling: external force on a test charge and the continuum force and power densities
current_object.statement:
Adopt as physical postulates of this framework, on the spacetime and particle model of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]] and [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]] and on the special-relativity particle model [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]]: (i) [Test charge in a prescribed external field] Let $q\in\mathbb R$ be a constant charge parameter ([[def-em-sources]]), $m>0$ an externally supplied rest mass, $x:J\to A$ a future timelike $C^2$ massive worldline with four-velocity $U$, and let $F$ be a prescribed field of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] that is $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of the graph of $x$ and is generated externally to the particle. Adopt the equation of motion

$$m\,\frac{dU}{d\tau}=q\,\Phi(U),$$

where $\Phi$ is the raised-index operator of the field at the event $x(\tau)$, defined by $\eta(\Phi(u),w)=F(w,u)$ ([[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]]); equivalently $m\,dU^\mu/d\tau=q\,F^{\mu\nu}U_\nu$. The particle's own field is excluded from $F$: this is the external-field coupling, and it defines no self-force. (ii) [Continuum matter coupling] For a smooth source $(\rho,J)$ of [[def-em-sources]] interacting with the field through an explicitly stated matter model to which this coupling applies, adopt the force density $\rho E+J\times B$ (unit N m$^{-3}$) and the power density $J\cdot E$ (unit W m$^{-3}$) as the electromagnetic source terms of that matter model; they describe the local interaction of the field with matter and are not a property of a prescribed current alone. (iii) [Scope] The rest mass and the charge are inputs; $m$ is not derived within electromagnetism. The coupling is adopted for constant $q$ and $m>0$; no magnetic-monopole coupling, no radiation reaction and no self-force are included. In particular the nonrelativistic coordinate statement $mr''=q(E+r'\times B)$ is not adopted as exact: the adopted statement is the covariant one of clause (i), and any low-speed statement requires its own approximation hypotheses and error bounds.
current_object.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem. The exposition must state the exact data (constant charge, externally supplied positive rest mass, future timelike C^2 worldline, prescribed external field C^1 near the graph), name the raised-index operator $\Phi$ with its defining identity and index form from [[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]] so that the equation is unambiguous, and state the exclusion of the particle's own field. Clause (ii) is a formulation premise for matter models, with its units fixed by [[def-em-si-conventions]] and its cross product the spatial one of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]; it is not a derivation from the field equations. Clause (iii) records the scope: no self-force, no radiation reaction, no magnetic monopole, and no exact Newtonian law. Empirical support for the coupling is a nonlogical relation of the framework; the item claims no verification and no measured value.

current_object.title: The microscopic vacuum Maxwell equations: smooth and weak branches
current_object.statement:
Adopt as a physical postulate of this framework the following four equations for the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and the sources of [[def-em-sources]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with $\mu_0>0$, $c>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and the SI units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. (a) [Smooth branch] Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^1$ fields with the additional derivatives required by each equation existing and continuous, and let $\rho,J$ be continuous. Then, with the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the partial derivative $\partial_t$ at fixed position of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]],

$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE.$$

(b) [Weak branch] Let instead $E,B$ be locally integrable $\mathbb R^3$-valued fields and $\rho,J$ locally integrable scalar and vector fields on $I\times\Omega$, identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]). Let $\operatorname{div}$, $\operatorname{curl}$ and $\partial_t$ act as distributional derivatives, and let $\psi$ range over $C_c^\infty(I\times\Omega)$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]). Then the same four identities hold in the sense of [[def-distribution]]: the pairings $\langle\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0,\psi\rangle$, $\langle\operatorname{div}B,\psi\rangle$, $\langle\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB,\psi\rangle$ and $\langle\operatorname{curl}B-\mu_0J-c^{-2}\partial_tE,\psi\rangle$ vanish for every such $\psi$, all derivatives being distributional derivatives ([[def-distributional-derivative]]). (c) [Scope] The postulate contains no magnetic charge: $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and no magnetic-source term appears in $\operatorname{curl}E$. Sources that are not locally integrable functions (point or sheet sources) are covered by neither branch and require their own definition. The equations are adopted classical vacuum physics in the named inertial chart; they are not deduced from charge conservation, from empirical agreement or from the special-relativity postulates, and this item by itself asserts no covariance under changes of inertial frame.
current_object.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem. Obligations and conventions: the fields and sources are those of [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-sources]], the operators are the published divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the partial derivative of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], and the weak reading uses exactly the regular-distribution embedding, the test space and the distributional derivative named in the statement. The exposition must state that the four equations are adopted, that the choice of the sign and constant conventions is the one fixed by [[def-em-si-conventions]], and that no magnetic charge is included; the sources not covered by either branch are excluded explicitly. Empirical support for Maxwell's equations is a nonlogical relation of the framework, not a proof, and no verification is claimed here.

current_object.title: The localized Newtonian potential and the ideal point-charge Coulomb field
current_object.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), inherited from the cited Lebesgue, polar, Newtonian and distribution interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]). Work in $\mathbb R^3$ with its Euclidean structure ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-metric-ball]]) and the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]], $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}>0$. Let $\Phi$ be the $n=3$ fundamental solution of $-\Delta$ of [[def-laplace-fundamental-solution-with-positive-minus-laplacian-sign]], normalised by $-\Delta T_\Phi=\delta_0$; then $\omega_2=4\pi$ and
$$\Phi(z)=\frac{1}{4\pi|z|}\qquad(z\ne0)$$
([[cor-volume-of-the-unit-n-ball]], [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]). Let $Nf$ be the Newtonian potential of [[def-newtonian-potential]].
(a) [Smooth compact sources] Let $\rho:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^1$ with compact support contained in $\overline B_R$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[def-metric-ball]]), put $\varphi:=\varepsilon_0^{-1}N\rho$ and $E:=-\nabla\varphi$. Then $\varphi\in C^2(\mathbb R^3)$ ([[thm-newtonian-potential-for-holder-data-is-classical]]), and pointwise on $\mathbb R^3$
$$-\Delta\varphi=\frac{\rho}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad \operatorname{div}E=\frac{\rho}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=0$$
with the operators of [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]] and [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]. Moreover, with $Q:=\int\rho\,d\lambda_3$, for every $x\in\mathbb R^3$ the absolutely convergent Coulomb integral representation holds, and its far-field bound holds for $|x|>2R$,
$$E(x)=\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{x-y}{|x-y|^3}\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y)\quad(x\in\mathbb R^3),\qquad |E(x)|\le\frac{\| \rho\|_1}{\pi\varepsilon_0|x|^2}\quad(|x|>2R),$$
and for $|x|>\max(2R,1)$ the potential obeys the decay bound $|\varphi(x)|\le\bigl(|Q|/(4\pi)+R\|\rho\|_1/\pi\bigr)/(\varepsilon_0|x|)$ ([[lem-em-newtonian-far-field-gradient]], [[thm-decay-of-the-newtonian-potential-of-compactly-supported-data]]). The pair $(E,0,\rho,0)$ therefore realises the pure electrostatic regime of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] with source $\rho$, and $E$ is the field of the localised Newtonian potential.
(b) [Uniqueness with vanishing at infinity] If $\psi\in C^2(\mathbb R^3)$ satisfies $-\Delta\psi=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ pointwise on $\mathbb R^3$ and $\lim_{|x|\to\infty}\psi(x)=0$, then $\psi=\varphi$ ([[thm-weak-maximum-principle-for-the-laplacian]]). In particular, among $C^2$ solutions of the Poisson equation of a compactly supported $C^1$ source decaying at infinity, the localised Newtonian potential is the unique one.
(c) [Compactly supported $L^1$ sources] If instead $\rho\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ is real, measurable and compactly supported, then $N\rho$ is finite $\lambda_3$-almost everywhere, belongs to $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^3)$, is $C^\infty$ and harmonic off the support of $\rho$, and its regular distribution satisfies
$$-\Delta T_{\varepsilon_0^{-1}N\rho}=T_{\rho/\varepsilon_0}\qquad\text{in }\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^3)$$
([[thm-newtonian-potential-solves-poisson-distributionally]], scaled by $\varepsilon_0^{-1}$; [[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]).
(d) [Point charge] Let $q\in\mathbb R$ and $x_0\in\mathbb R^3$ and define, with arbitrary values at $x_0$,
$$\varphi_q(x):=\frac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0|x-x_0|},\qquad E_q(x):=\frac{q\,(x-x_0)}{4\pi\varepsilon_0|x-x_0|^3}\qquad(x\ne x_0).$$
Then $\varphi_q\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^3)$, $E_q$ is locally integrable and $C^\infty$ off $x_0$, $E_q=-\nabla\varphi_q$ on $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{x_0\}$, and, with $T_{\varphi_q}$ the regular distribution of $\varphi_q$ and $\operatorname{div}E_q:=\sum_i\partial_iT_{E_{q,i}}$, $\operatorname{curl}E_q:=(\partial_2T_{E_{q,3}}-\partial_3T_{E_{q,2}},\ \partial_3T_{E_{q,1}}-\partial_1T_{E_{q,3}},\ \partial_1T_{E_{q,2}}-\partial_2T_{E_{q,1}})$,
$$-\Delta T_{\varphi_q}=\frac{q}{\varepsilon_0}\delta_{x_0},\qquad \operatorname{div}E_q=\frac{q}{\varepsilon_0}\delta_{x_0},\qquad \operatorname{curl}E_q=0\qquad\text{in }\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^3)$$
([[thm-minus-laplacian-of-the-fundamental-solution-is-dirac]] for the first identity, [[lem-em-distributional-gradient-smooth-off-a-point]] for the passage from the potential to the field, [[def-distributional-derivative]], [[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]). The distribution $q\delta_{x_0}$ is the fixed-time reading of the stationary point charge of [[def-em-weak-sources]](b) with charge parameter $q$ and constant trajectory $z\equiv x_0$ ([[def-em-electrostatic-regime]](e)); so the pair $(E_q,0)$ satisfies the distributional pure electrostatic equations with that point source. This is an idealised point-source model: no claim of uniqueness for the point source, no self-force and no statement about the field at $x_0$ itself is made.

current_object.physical_scope: Classical electrostatics in vacuum for a compactly supported charge density (smooth $C^1$ or merely $L^1$), with the localised Newtonian potential $\varphi=\varepsilon_0^{-1}N\rho$ and its field $E=-\nabla\varphi$; in the smooth case the field is the continuous Coulomb integral, the potential is the unique decaying $C^2$ solution of $-\Delta\varphi=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, and $(E,0,\rho,0)$ realises the pure electrostatic regime. The point-charge clause states the distributional identities for the idealised singular source $q\delta_{x_0}$ in the framework's SI conventions, with no uniqueness, self-force, reaction or empirical claim.

current_object.title: Well-posed weak solvability and classical regularity for declared smooth-domain elliptic boundary problems
current_object.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice as declared by the weak-solvability lemmas. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]] is the local graph definition used throughout), let $\varepsilon\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega;\operatorname{Sym}^3)$ be uniformly positive ($\alpha|\xi|^2\le\xi\cdot\varepsilon(x)\xi\le eta|\xi|^2$ on $\Omega$ for some $0<\alpha\le eta<\infty$), and let $ho$ be smooth on $\overline\Omega$. Then:
(a) **Dirichlet.** For every $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$ there is exactly one weak solution $u\in H^1(\Omega)$ with trace $g$ of $\int_\Omega
abla v\cdot\varepsilon
abla u=\int_\Omegaho v$ for all $v\in H_0^1(\Omega)$; it depends continuously on the data, is $C^\infty$ on $\overline\Omega$, and satisfies $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon
abla u)=ho$ pointwise with $u|_{\partial\Omega}=g$.
(b) **Neumann.** For every smooth outward conormal datum $g$ satisfying $\int_{\Omega_j}ho\,dx+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}g\,dS=0$ on every connected component $\Omega_j$ of $\Omega$, there is a weak solution of $\int_\Omega
abla v\cdot\varepsilon
abla u=\int_\Omegaho v+\int_{\partial\Omega}g\,Tv$ for all $v\in H^1(\Omega)$. It is unique up to a separately chosen additive constant on each component, and imposing $\int_{\Omega_j}u=0$ for each component gives a unique normalised solution, smooth on each closed component. In particular on a connected domain the compatibility is $\int_{\partial\Omega}g=-\int_\Omegaho$, with a single additive constant.
(c) **Transmission.** For the stated finitely many disjoint closed smooth interfaces strictly inside $\Omega$, piecewise smooth uniformly positive $\varepsilon$, piecewise smooth bulk $ho$ and smooth sheet charge $\sigma$, prescribe either the smooth outer Dirichlet datum of (a), or the smooth outer Neumann datum of (b). The weak right-hand side includes $\int_\Omegaho v+\sum_\Gamma\int_\Gamma\sigma\,Tv$ and, in the Neumann case, $\int_{\partial\Omega}g\,Tv$. With outer Dirichlet data the globally $H^1$ solution is unique. With outer Neumann data it exists exactly when the total right-hand side vanishes on the constant of each connected component, equivalently $\int_{\Omega_j}ho+\sum_{\Gamma\subset\Omega_j}\int_\Gamma\sigma+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}g=0$ for each $j$, and is unique modulo componentwise constants; zero componentwise means give uniqueness. In either case the equal one-sided traces and $C^\infty$ regularity on each closed side hold, and the flux jump is $n\cdot[\varepsilon
abla u]=-\sigma$ in the sign convention of [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]].
Edge and junction points, reentrant corners, coefficient loss of regularity and general piecewise classical regularity beyond finitely many disjoint smooth interfaces are excluded. The existence content is that of the two weak solvability lemmas; this item states the combined existence-and-regularity theorem on the declared domains.
current_object.strategy: The claim collects three recorded branches and their compatibility. (a) Existence, uniqueness, exact prescribed trace and continuous dependence are [[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]]; the classical upgrade to $C^\infty$ on the closure, with the classical equation and boundary values, is [[lem-em-smooth-domain-elliptic-regularity]]. (b) Testing the displayed weak identity with the constant on each component gives $\int_{\Omega_j}\rho+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}g=0$, including the minus sign when solved for the outer conormal integral. Necessity of componentwise compatibility, existence, uniqueness modulo componentwise constants and the normalised form are [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]]; the classical upgrade is again [[lem-em-smooth-domain-elliptic-regularity]]. (c) Apply the transmission functional including the sheet-charge term, with outer Dirichlet tests in $H_0^1$ for full uniqueness, or outer Neumann tests in $H^1$ with that functional zero on every componentwise constant and the chosen mean normalisation. The weak existence and the one-sided trace identity are the transmission part of [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]], the two-sided classical smoothness and the jump relation are [[lem-em-smooth-domain-elliptic-regularity]], and the passage from the weak identity to the interface flux uses the divergence theorem for the piecewise smooth configuration together with the first Green identity [[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]. The smooth coefficients, conormal field and chart changes are smooth by the calculus conventions of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] and [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]; the inner products and the quadratic form $\nabla v\cdot\varepsilon\nabla u$ use the Euclidean inner product [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. No existence or regularity claim is made beyond the stated smooth-domain, finite-interface regime.

current_object.title: Spectral completeness of the declared PEC waveguide and cavity classes
current_object.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the explicitly used variational, Sobolev and compact-spectral suppliers. Let the PEC classes be those of [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]]: for a bounded $C^\infty$ domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$, $X$ is the graph-norm closure in $H(\operatorname{curl})\cap H(\operatorname{div})$ of the smooth fields on the closure with $n\times u=0$, $V=\{u\in X:\operatorname{div}u=0\}$ and $H=\overline V^{\,L^2}$. Then:
(a) **Smooth cavity.** The curl form on $V$ has a complete orthonormal $L^2$ eigenbasis $\{u_j\}$ with nonnegative eigenvalues $\lambda_j$ of finite multiplicity, $\lambda_j\to\infty$ whenever $H$ is infinite dimensional, and a finite-dimensional zero eigenspace that is retained; the eigen-equation $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u_j=\lambda_ju_j$ holds distributionally with the PEC trace. The associated second-order wave with initial displacement in $V$ and velocity in $H$ has coefficients $a_j''+c^2\lambda_ja_j=0$, converges in $C_tV\cap C_tH$ for finite-energy data, and retains the finitely many $\lambda=0$ modes $a_j(t)=a_j(0)+ta_j'(0)$. The classical smoothness of the eigenfields on the declared smooth domain, and the solvability of the shifted auxiliary boundary problems used in the construction, are those supplied by [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]] on $\Omega$.
(b) **Rectangular class.** For a rectangular box the separable products described in the mode verification are dense in the reflection-parity energy class, and every initial datum of that class has a unique $C(\mathbb R;L^2)$ weak solution of $\partial_tE=(\varepsilon\mu)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}B$, $\partial_tB=-\operatorname{curl}E$ in the class with constant energy, with finite separated modes dense at every time. The rectangular statements are the recorded rectangular reflection-class completeness lemma [[lem-em-rectangular-pec-energy-completeness]] (the $G2$ branch); the individual TE/TM mode verification against the Maxwell equations and the PEC conditions is the recorded $G1$ physics branch, homed on the physical guide page and not consumed here as a mathematical premise. No completeness in lossy, open-ended or non-smooth classes is asserted.
current_object.strategy: The smooth-cavity assertions are exactly [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]], whose proof constructs the compact self-adjoint solution operator of the shifted problem with the coercive solver and the smooth-domain interior estimate, applies the compact self-adjoint spectral theorem to obtain the eigenbasis and the multiplicities, and derives the distributional eigen-equation and the modal wave expansion with zero modes retained. This item records the composition with the elliptic existence theorem of this page: [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]] supplies the weak solvability and the classical ($C^\infty$-on-the-closure) upgrade on the bounded smooth domain for the elliptic boundary problems used in the closure argument, so the eigenfields and the auxiliary problems live on the declared smooth class; the quadratic graph forms and the curl/div expressions are computed with the calculus conventions of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]] and the Euclidean inner product [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. The rectangular assertions are the recorded $G2$ content of [[lem-em-rectangular-pec-energy-completeness]]: the reflection parities convert the boundary class into a rectangular torus class, the imported one-dimensional complete trigonometric system and Hilbert Fourier expansion give product completeness, and the finite-dimensional Fourier ODE with conservation of $\varepsilon|\hat E|^2+|\hat B|^2/\mu$ gives the unique weak solution and energy conservation; the direct TE/TM mode verification is the recorded physics branch G1 on the guide page and is not a mathematical dependency here. The recorded K10 branch (uniform Ohmic loss) is a physical-model branch of the same modal argument and is homed on the physical page, not here.
